steps.description: Fit DESeq2 with design ~condition + time + condition:time on the pre-filtered count matrix (genes with >=10 counts in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size). Set explicit reference levels for condition and time and report them. Test the condition:time interaction coefficient with the Wald test as the primary result. Also extract the simple effects: the condition effect at the reference time level (main effect coefficient) and the condition effect at the other time level (main effect + interaction, via a named contrast). Shrink all three effect estimates (interaction contrast and both simple-effect contrasts) with ashr, since none is a single model coefficient that apeglm could take. Keep both the unshrunken and shrunken log2FC plus lfcSE in the output tables. Apply DESeq2's independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within each of the three contrasts separately at alpha=0.05; do not pool p-values across contrasts. Flag genes with NA adjusted p-values from count-outlier detection (Cook's distance) separately from those removed by independent filtering. State explicitly: Salmon-derived counts with no quant.sf/length table accompanying them means the length-scaling correction cannot be confirmed — proceed on counts as delivered and note that isoform-usage shifts could appear as apparent DE. State the power limitation of the interaction test at n=3 replicates per cell (a difference-of-differences with larger SE than either main effect at the same n).

plan.title: Treatment x time-point interaction DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 2 time points (t0, t1) with 3 replicates per cell (12 samples, single batch), raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes). The research question — does the treatment effect differ between time points — is an interaction question, not a simple two-group comparison. We first run sample-structure QC to confirm the samples cluster by condition/time before fitting any model and to check for outliers given the small n. We fit DESeq2 with design ~condition*time (interaction), test the condition:time interaction coefficient with the Wald test as the primary result, and report the simple effects (treatment effect at t0, treatment effect at t1) alongside it, since the interaction coefficient alone cannot say whether an effect exists at either time point and a simple effect alone cannot say whether it differs across time. Because this is Salmon-derived output with no accompanying quant.sf/length data, we cannot confirm length-scaling was applied — this is flagged so the model does not silently assume a gene-length offset. With only 3 replicates per cell, the interaction test (a difference-of-differences) has materially lower power than a main effect; we shrink log fold changes with ashr (contrast-level shrinkage, since the interaction/simple-effect contrasts are not single model coefficients), enforce independent filtering + BH FDR at alpha 0.05 within each contrast, and state the power limitation explicitly rather than loosening thresholds. Enrichment (fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic) runs per contrast (interaction, simple effect at t0, simple effect at t1) against MSigDB Hallmark (present locally) then Reactome (present locally) as a second collection, never pooling contrasts. The final report synthesizes fit diagnostics, the three-way contrast table (simple effects + interaction), enrichment per contrast, and a reproducibility record, with explicit power caveats for the n=3/cell interaction design.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

With an interaction question and three or fewer replicates in a cell of the design, the interaction term has low power. The interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, thus its standard error is larger than the standard error of a main effect at the same replicate number. Keep the interaction test as the primary result, but report the simple effects in each level beside it, with the same threshold. State the power limit in the report, and do not loosen the threshold to compensate. A gene that is absent from the interaction list is not shown to have the same effect in both levels.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
